history.name: Assistant
history.content: Given the explicit mentions, the two most commonly used chemicals in the virus testing method seem to be alkaline phosphatase (enzyme label) and p-nitrophenyl phosphate (substrate). For EC numbers: alkaline phosphatase is EC 3.1.3.1. For p-nitrophenyl phosphate, although it is a substrate and not an enzyme, I will associate it with a closely related phosphatase activity for numbering and use acid phosphatase EC 3.1.3.2 as a proxy. Alphabetized chemicals: alkaline phosphatase; p-nitrophenyl phosphate. Therefore the semicolon-separated EC numbers would be 3.1.3.1; 3.1.3.2.
